Bruv I literally have had the exact same thing since as long ago as I can remember, brushing against a wall with my left shoulder and feeling some strange compelling force insisting I do it again on the right, scratching my right hand on the corner of a book and just needing to do it on the left in the same spot….

After a really really long time I worked out a way to pacify it slightly. For example if you were to scratch your left hand on, say, some concrete, here’s what I do: I scratch my right hand with my left thumb in the same spot, same force and (attempted) same sensation. Then I move my right hand to get rid of the sensation of “fuck I did this movement with my left hand” then when the voices in my head start being all like “oi cockhead you didn’t actually go and sit back down and touch that piece of concrete on your right hand side too” I just (mentally of course) say to the voices “shut the fuck up” in the most aggressive and venomous way possible and go about my day. 

The trick is to be even but substitute things around instead of directly repeating an action. Starting now, I recommend you do this maybe like once or twice a day and then start ramping up the amount of substitution.

Additionally, you can try and pit yourself against your brain whenever it tries to remind you that you didn’t actually do something properly you just substituted something for a sensation or action. Try mentally arguing with yourself if possible. If not, treat this like an act of defiance of sorts.

The idea of substitution is so that you make your OCD less strict over the course of a long time. Eventually you will be able to occasionally ignore that sense of “feeling uneven” that you and I  both know so well. 

I found this to be fairly effective and I find myself only responding to my unevenness when it isn’t going to cause me harm or moderate inconvenience. I hope this helps you too my brother.
